title: BRICS Parliamentary Forum condemns Pahalgam terror attack, seeks UNSC reforms
syllabus: GS2 › Important international institutions and groupings (BRICS, UN) · GS3 › Terrorism; Linkages between state and non-state actors
summary: The 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum in New Delhi adopted a declaration condemning the Pahalgam attack and cross-border terrorism, and calling for UN and Security Council reform.
ideas: Diplomatic gain: BRICS parliaments, including China and Iran, condemned Pahalgam and cross-border terrorism in one text.
GS2 · BRICS / India's diplomacy
At the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum (New Delhi, 2026), members including China and Iran condemned the Pahalgam attack and cross-border terrorism.
India's counter-terror agenda endorsed: zero tolerance, no double standards, no link between terror and religion, and quick adoption of the CCIT.
GS3 · Terrorism
The BRICS declaration backed India's call for zero tolerance, no double standards and early adoption of the Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism.
Reform of global governance: BRICS calls for comprehensive UN reform, including the Security Council, and stronger multilateralism.
GS2 · International institutions
BRICS parliaments called for comprehensive reform of the UN, including the Security Council, echoing India's long-standing demand.
Parliamentary diplomacy: legislators, not just governments, carry India's positions to other countries.
GS2 · Diplomacy
Hosting the BRICS Parliamentary Forum shows parliamentary diplomacy amplifying India's positions on terror and UN reform.

title: Climate justice needs quicker compensation: first Loss and Damage payout to Nepal
syllabus: GS3 › Environment; Disaster management · GS2 › International institutions; India's neighbourhood · GS4 › Ethical issues in international funding
context: The UN's Fund for Loss and Damage has allocated $21.6 million (about Rs 190 crore) to Nepal, nearly two months after devastating floods. It is the first time the Fund has earmarked a grant for a disaster-affected nation. The Indian Express argues the episode should become a case study for reforming the Fund.
ideas: Loss and damage is compensation, not charity, because it rests on responsibility for climate change.
GS3 climate · GS2 global governance
Loss and damage finance is compensation owed, not charity, because it rests on responsibility for emissions.
Speed is justice: delays raise hardship and rebuilding costs, especially for poor countries.
GS3 DM · GS4 fairness
Delayed climate compensation is justice denied: it raises hardship and rebuilding costs.
Money is short: $822 million pledged, about a third of pending claims.
GS3 · Climate finance
The Loss and Damage Fund has only $822 million pledged, about a third of pending claims.

summary: The UN Fund for Loss and Damage made its first grant, to flood-hit Nepal; the Indian Express says payouts must be faster and the Fund reformed.
evolution: Fund for Loss and Damage created at COP27, after a nearly three-decade campaign by vulnerable nations.
First grant earmarked, to Nepal; developed countries insisted it is an exception, not a precedent.
COP31 begins in Antalya, Turkey, with compensation on the agenda.
